articles.title: Trump EPA moves to wipe out climate rules for power plants
articles.text:
On the heels of the hottest summer on record and a United Nations report warning that global temperatures are likely to push climate risks to “increasingly dangerous heights,” the Trump administration overturned most of a Biden-era rule limiting climate pollution from power plants, the second-largest source of greenhouse gas emissions.
The Environmental Protection Agency announced a final plan Monday that guts the 2024 Carbon Pollution Standards, which the agency said exceeds its authority under the Clean Air Act by requiring control technologies “that are not adequately demonstrated.” The agency also proposed revoking “all remaining GHG emissions requirements for power plants,” arguing their emissions “have no material impact on climate change.”
The plan to revoke the Carbon Pollution Standards was initially revealed last spring.
In 2007, the Supreme Court ruled that the Clean Air Act’s definition of air pollutants includes greenhouse gases, which cause climate change, and that if the EPA concludes that GHGs pose a danger to human health and the environment, it must act to reduce those emissions. The EPA made that “endangerment finding” in 2009.
“The Trump administration is now kicking the legs out from under the entire legal framework for regulating climate pollution by arguing that climate pollution does not harm human health or welfare,” said Zealan Hoover, a former senior advisor to the EPA during the Biden administration.
Hoover and other environmental and climate experts have not yet had a chance to review the specific arguments the agency is making to justify its actions.
Maggie Coulter, senior attorney at the Center for Biological Diversity’s Climate Law Institute, expects the Trump administration to make a “non-endangerment finding” so they don’t have to regulate greenhouse gas emissions at all. “That goes against really well-established science,” Coulter said. “Will this stand up in court? We would argue, definitely not.”

articles.title: The UK's £100 billion data center boom is suffering from a major bottleneck that puts capacity and performance at risk
articles.text:
The UK's £100 billion data center boom is suffering from a major bottleneck that puts capacity and performance at risk
Cabling is holding back the UK data center boom
- The UK data center boom is being held back by cabling bottlenecks, a survey of senior data center decision-makers has found
- AI is also progressing so quickly that data centers often require upgrades almost immediately after becoming operational
- Findings suggest UK data centers are not actually being built to perform
As the United Kingdom seeks to establish itself as a leader in AI tech, the buildout of data centers is encountering one key obstacle.
AI technologies are advancing so rapidly that developers are struggling to futureproof data centers to be able to handle the additional capacity or new computing requirements.
According to a survey by data center infrastructure specialist Onnec, data centers are struggling to navigate past cabling, latency, and rapidly advancing AI capacity requirements that take years to fix.
UK data centers are struggling to stay fit for purpose
Onnec found over three-quarters (77%) of UK data center operators were encountering critical bottlenecks in sourcing cabling to support their AI workloads, with 72% stating that the AI rush is creating additional cabling problems that could take years to fix. Furthermore, 37% of data center operators are encountering latency or bottleneck issues with AI training.
But the problems don’t end there. These trends are being worsened by the rapid development of AI technology. 65% stated that alongside these problems, their data centers are seeing AI capacity increase.
Moreover, 83% also stated that by the time their hardware is operational, AI requirements have progressed so much that upgrades are needed almost immediately to meet new demands and capacity. This compounds problems with cabling bottlenecks, with a further 33% unable to scale their data centers without significant cabling work.
In some cases cables have introduced significant project delays or additional costs, with 44% stating that insufficient upfront cabling planning had caused such issues.

“Everyone is focused on securing power and GPUs for AI, but the network connecting that hardware together is too often finalised only after those decisions have already been made,” said Matt Salter, Global Head of Data Centres at Onnec.
“The racks are set, the pathways are tight, and teams are left working around the design. You can have the power and GPUs in place, but they still need to communicate. If the network cannot support that traffic, the AI environment will not perform as expected.”
“The priority is to make cabling part of the design before layouts and pathways are fixed,” adds Salter. “Operators need enough capacity, access and flexibility to support more than the first hardware deployment. Otherwise, today's AI build-out will leave teams carrying out expensive work inside live facilities much sooner than expected.”

articles.title: US data centers could consume more natural gas than Germany and Japan combined by 2035 | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The AI race has grown so frenzied that, by 2035, U.S. data centers are projected to consume more natural gas than Germany and Japan combined.
Over the next decade, data centers are expected to be the second-strongest driver of natural gas demand growth after LNG exports. The facilities could consume about 18 billion cubic feet per day, according to a new report from BloombergNEF, nearly double the amount the organization predicted just nine months ago.
The new forecast takes into account that not all announced data center projects will be completed.
Data centers that produce power onsite have grabbed headlines in recent months, with Meta, Microsoft, Google, and Amazon all announcing plans for new natural gas power plants that will bypass the grid. Projects such as these will consume 2.9 billion to 3.4 billion cubic feet per day by 2035. That’s about as much as all data centers consume today, including natural gas used to generate power for the grid.
But onsite-powered data centers could represent just a fraction of overall demand growth, according to BloombergNEF.
By the middle of the next decade, grid-connected data centers are predicted to drive an additional 15 billion cubic feet per day of natural gas consumption by the power sector. To put that in context, that’s five times more demand growth through 2035 than from all other grid-connected sectors combined.
If that stunning demand growth materializes, it could nudge natural gas prices higher.
Much of today’s data center buildout relies on stable natural gas prices, which have prevailed in recent years. But analysts at Noreva think that might be a false hope. The combined impact of the data center boom and rising LNG exports could cause prices to soar. Even if tech companies’ balance sheets can bear such a surge, utility ratepayers might not be able to.
Then there’s the climate impact.
Burning one cubic foot of natural gas releases the equivalent of 60 grams of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, including extraction, processing, and distribution, according to the IEA. The additional demand from data centers will generate 1 million metric tons more greenhouse gas pollution daily. That’s about 12% of total U.S. greenhouse gas emissions today.

articles.title: Rogers to offer 150+ NHL games for free to select TV customers
articles.text:
Rogers is adding a bunch of new National Hockey League (NHL) content to its Xfinity TV service for free.
According to an announcement from the telecom, Rogers will add exclusive Sportsnet+ content to TV packages at no additional cost, including over 150 NHL games and Monday Night Hockey. The addition starts on Sept. 29.
Customers who have TV packages with Sportsnet will be able to access three new digital channels that will feature the Sportsnet+ content. According to Rogers, the Sportsnet+ add-on package, valued at $12.99/mo, will be included automatically for eligible customers.
Rogers says customers won’t need to take any action to make this happen and will simply be able to access it using their remote later this month.
Based on the details on Rogers website, the free Sportsnet+ content will be available with the company’s Plus and Ultimate TV plans. Currently, Plus TV costs $55/mo when paired with home internet (full bundle price starts at $130/mo). That plan includes up to 120 channels, a TV box and voice remote, access to Rogers’ Xfinity Stream app, sports, news, and more.
Meanwhile, the Ultimate TV plan costs $95 when bundled with home internet (full bundle price starts at $170/mo). It includes everything in Plus, but with up to 170 channels and additional sports and new content. Ultimate also includes Rogers’ StreamSaver, a bundle of streaming services including Netflix (with ads), Disney+ (with ads) and Apple TV+.
Notably, Rogers’ free Sportsnet offer comes after CBC ended Hockey Night in Canada in June following the expiry of its sublicensing deal with Rogers’ Sportsnet. Further, Rogers raised the price of its Sportsnet+ subscription in July after it signed a deal to purchase the remaining 25 per cent stake in Maple Leaf Sports and Entertainment (MLSE) that same month.

articles.title: Última oportunidad en PS Plus: Un aclamado juego de terror y 7 títulos más dirán adiós en octubre
articles.text:
PlayStation Plus retirará ocho videojuegos de sus catálogos Extra y Premium en octubre, entre ellos Silent Hill 2 Remake, Yakuza: Like a Dragon y Jurassic World Evolution 2. Los suscriptores de PlayStation 5 y PlayStation 4 aún podrán acceder a estos títulos hasta el 20 de octubre, antes de que abandonen el servicio.
La actualización importa porque el catálogo de PS Plus funciona con un sistema de rotación. Los juegos están disponibles mientras mantengan su presencia en el servicio, por lo que una suscripción activa no garantiza el acceso permanente. La salida de Silent Hill 2 Remake concentra la atención por tratarse de una de las producciones de terror más reconocidas de los últimos años.
PUBLICIDAD
Los ocho juegos que abandonarán el servicio el 20 de octubre
PlayStation actualizó la sección “abandonarán pronto” para confirmar los títulos que desaparecerán del catálogo durante la segunda mitad de octubre. La lista reúne producciones de terror psicológico, rol, estrategia, simulación y juegos independientes.
Estos son los videojuegos que dejarán PS Plus:
- Silent Hill 2 Remake
- Yakuza: Like a Dragon
- Jurassic World Evolution 2
- Death Squared
- Rogue Lords
- Gloomhaven Mercenaries Edition
- Harvest Moon: Light of Hope Special Edition
- Lake
Los usuarios de los niveles Extra y Premium pueden instalar y jugar estos títulos sin coste adicional mientras sigan disponibles. Después del 20 de octubre, será necesario comprarlos para acceder a ellos, salvo que regresen al catálogo en el futuro.
PUBLICIDAD
Silent Hill 2 Remake encabeza las salidas de octubre
Silent Hill 2 Remake, desarrollado por Bloober Team y publicado por Konami, es el título más destacado entre las bajas. El juego recuperó una de las historias más asociadas al terror psicológico y obtuvo una calificación de 86 en Metacritic.
La obra original llegó en 2001, desarrollada por Team Silent. Su trama sigue a James Sunderland, quien llega a la ciudad de Silent Hill después de recibir una carta de Mary, su esposa fallecida. La narrativa se centra en la culpa, el duelo, la represión y el deterioro emocional del protagonista.
PUBLICIDAD
La ciudad funciona como una representación de la mente de James. Criaturas, entornos y personajes responden a sus traumas, mientras Pyramid Head encarna la búsqueda de castigo del protagonista. El uso de niebla, sombras y la música de Akira Yamaoka construyó una identidad que influyó en posteriores juegos de terror.
El título también introdujo finales que dependen de acciones del jugador, más allá de decisiones explícitas. Aspectos como la atención a determinados objetos o la forma de cuidar la salud del personaje pueden alterar el desenlace.
PUBLICIDAD
Yakuza: Like a Dragon es otro de los juegos que dejará la suscripción. El proyecto de Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio y SEGA cambió el sistema de combate de acción de la saga por una estructura de rol, con enfrentamientos por turnos y un nuevo protagonista.
Jurassic World Evolution 2, de Frontier Developments, propone la construcción y administración de un parque de dinosaurios. El jugador debe gestionar instalaciones, especies y recursos dentro de un simulador basado en la franquicia cinematográfica.
PUBLICIDAD
El resto de la lista suma experiencias de diferentes escalas. Death Squared plantea puzles cooperativos; Rogue Lords se apoya en decisiones estratégicas; Gloomhaven Mercenaries Edition adapta el juego de mesa de fantasía; Harvest Moon: Light of Hope Special Edition recupera mecánicas de vida rural, y Lake presenta una historia centrada en una repartidora de correo.
PS Plus recibió diez juegos durante septiembre
Las salidas coinciden con la llegada de nuevos títulos al servicio. PlayStation añadió diez juegos para los suscriptores de Extra y Premium, incluidos WWE 2K26, Metro Redux y Mega Man X Command Mission.
PUBLICIDAD
La lista incorpora además RuneScape: Dragonwilds, Ball x Pit, Date Everything!, Slitterhead, Ninja Gaiden: Ragebound, Dungeons of Hinterberg y Sniper Elite: Resistance. PlayStation también adelantó la futura llegada de Mycopunk, Dino Crisis 2 y el primer Ratchet & Clank.
La rotación del catálogo obliga a revisar los juegos marcados como “abandonarán pronto”. Silent Hill 2 Remake y los otros siete títulos permanecerán disponibles hasta el 20 de octubre para los suscriptores que quieran terminarlos o probarlos antes de su retirada.

articles.title: Un pueblo de 600 habitantes tiene una estación de AVE por la que no pasa ni un solo tren. Conectarla a la red cuesta 1.700 millones
articles.text:
Año 2006.
Las máquinas llegan al terreno y empiezan a remover la tierra. Dos décadas después, la obra no está terminada. ¿De qué estamos hablando? Con esos datos, podríamos hablar de muchas carreteras. Y de muchas conexiones ferroviarias. Esta vez hablamos de la Y vasca. Un proyecto que lleva más de 20 años en desarrollo y del que, desde luego, no se atisba un final.
Y sin embargo, sí que tiene una certeza: un pueblo de 600 habitantes con una estación de AVE en la que se han gastado decenas de millones de euros y que puede morir sin que haya pasado un solo tren por ella.
¿Qué es la Y vasca? La Y vasca es el proyecto de alta velocidad ferroviaria que pretende unir las tres capitales de provincia del País Vasco. El objetivo es lanzar una línea de tren desde San Sebastián que se desdoble para llegar a Vitoria por un lado y a Bilbao por otro. De esta manera, Bilbao quedaría unido por alta velocidad a Francia pasando por San Sebastián e Irún y Vitoria, además, quedaría unida a Madrid mediante su conexión por la línea de Burgos.
Eso es lo que dice la teoría porque 20 años después de que las primeras máquinas empezaran a mover la tierra, el proyecto de la Y vasca sigue siendo una promesa más que una realidad. Y lo peor de todo, nadie tiene muy claro algunos de los puntos cruciales. Uno de ellos tiene una estación de tren abandonada junto a un pueblo de apenas 600 habitantes.
La conexión navarra. Además de las conexiones entre Francia y Bilbao o Vitoria y esta última con Madrid a través de Burgos, la Y Vasca tiene otra oportunidad: conectar con Pamplona. Esta última es mucho más que una simple conexión para pasajeros ya que se trata del enlace que pretende unir este tramo ferroviario de alta velocidad con el corredor del Mediterráneo pero también quedar unido al corredor Atlántico.
De salir adelante, la conexión será clave ya que permitiría mover mercancías y pasajeros con mucha facilidad entre el norte y el este español, solucionando en parte la dependencia radial que sufre gran parte del entramado ferroviario del país. Para muestra de esto último, el enlace entre Almería y Murcia.
Ezkio-Itsaso. Es la parada de Ezkio-Itsaso donde se concentra gran parte del meollo. Esta población de 604 habitantes, según el último censo publicado, vio cómo en 2022 por fin se terminó (más o menos) la magnífica estación de tren para la alta velocidad junto a la AP-636. Ahora, unos pocos minutos en coche separan sus idílicas casas en el monte de una estación de tren de alta velocidad.
Eso sí, de trenes, ni rastro. De hecho, los habitantes de este municipio corren el riesgo de no ver ni uno solo de ellos y comprobar qué sucede cuando construyes una enorme estación de tren y la dejas completamente abandonada. Hoy, cuentan en El Mundo, por allí sólo se dejan caer los grafiteros que comparten protagonismo con la maleza que quiere ganar terreno.
1.000 millones de euros en juego. Y es que aunque los operarios terminaron las obras en 2022, hay un problema: nadie confirmó este enlace. Es decir, la estación se ha construido pero desde entonces (y desde antes) se debate si el enlace para unir Pamplona con la Y vasca debe pasar por este municipio o, por el contrario, debería salir desde Vitoria.
Los motivos para dudar son evidentes. Si el tren pasa por Ezkio-Itsaso se calcula que la inversión en infraestructura costará unos 1.705 millones de euros. Sin embargo, para sacar adelante el enlace desde Vitoria apenas habría que invertir 585 millones de euros. Apenas, por decir algo.
Aralar. El nombre que explica este enorme sobrecoste se llama Aralar. Y es que tirar la línea por esta pequeña localidad reduciría el tiempo de viaje entre la Y vasca y Pamplona en 25 minutos. Pero la orografía es delicada. Primero porque habría que picar suelo en esta sierra hasta construir un túnel con líneas ferroviarias en ambos sentidos, así como todas las ramificaciones subterráneas adyacentes que son necesarias para garantizar la seguridad.
En total, se calcula que serían 21 kilómetros de excavaciones solo para el túnel ferroviario y hay numerosas incógnitas de qué se encontrarían los operarios sobre el terreno. Y es que no está del todo claro cuánto tiempo podría llevar la obra completa ni si existen más sobre costes. Tantos son los problemas que ya hay en marcha un estudio para una tercera vía.
El proyecto, además, cuenta con el rechazo frontal de organizaciones ambientalistas y los partidos políticos que más se inclinan por conservar el paisaje tal y como está.
Vitoria. La alternativa que está sobre la mesa es, como decíamos, la vía vitoriana que según El Mundo es la que tienen decidida en Transportes. En este caso el trayecto pasaría de 44 minutos a 69 minutos de viaje pero la orografía es mucho más amable por lo que no es necesario excavar tanta tierra. Es más barato pero, evidentemente, el tiempo de viaje es muy superior.
Los defensores de la vía Ezkio-Itsaso defienden que alargar el tiempo de viaje esos 25 minutos puede ser clave para que el tramo ferroviario fracase pese a sacarlo adelante. Quienes apuestan por la vía vitoriana alegan, evidentemente, menor impacto medioambiental y económico.
Sea como sea, lo que es seguro es que una estación ya está levantada. La duda es si caerá en desgracia y los habitantes de un pequeño pueblo guipuzcoano se quedarán con una moles de hormigón valorada en cuatro millones de euros para que por ella no pase ni un solo tren de alta velocidad.

articles.title: « Appuyez sur la touche 1 » : ne tombez surtout pas dans le piège de cette arnaque
articles.text:
Une auditrice de la radio ICI lance l’alerte : des appels automatiques tentent de vous mettre en contact direct avec des arnaqueurs. Pour y parvenir, il est indiqué aux victimes qu’un paiement suspect a été identifié sur leur compte en banque et qu’elles doivent appuyer sur la touche 1 de leur smartphone afin d’être mises en relation avec un soi-disant service des fraudes. Mais c’est précisément à ce moment-là que le piège se referme sur la victime.
« Taper 1 pour entrer en contact avec le service des fraudes » : attention à cette arnaque téléphonique
Cette arnaque débute par un simple appel téléphonique. À l’autre bout du fil, un serveur vocal vous avertit qu’un paiement suspect a été détecté sur votre compte en banque. Afin de bloquer ce soi-disant paiement, ou de vérifier que vous en êtes bien à l’origine, il vous est conseillé d’entrer en contact avec un service des fraudes en appuyant sur la touche 1 de votre téléphone.
C’est précisément à ce moment que le piège se referme. Craignant que son compte en banque ait été piraté, la victime peut être tentée d’appuyer sur la touche 1 de son téléphone. Le problème : cette touche ne renvoie en aucun cas vers un service des fraudes. En réalité, elle met en contact direct la victime avec un faux conseiller bancaire. Ce dernier cherchera ensuite à soutirer des informations confidentielles à la victime (numéro de carte bancaire, mot de passe, etc.), prétextant vouloir résoudre la situation au plus vite.
C’est précisément ce qui est arrivé ce 15 août à une auditrice de la radio ICI. Celle-ci a reçu un appel enregistré provenant prétendument du Crédit Mutuel et faisant état d’un soi-disant paiement suspect de 475,17 euros chez Zalando. Heureusement, elle a eu le réflexe de couper court à l’appel, étant donné qu’elle n’est pas cliente du Crédit Mutuel.
Comment ne pas tomber dans le piège de ce type d’arnaque ?
Pour rappel, une banque ne vous demandera jamais de communiquer par téléphone vos informations bancaires personnelles. Si vous avez le moindre doute, rendez-vous à un guichet physique de votre banque ou vérifiez tout simplement vos relevés de compte disponibles en ligne. Si aucun paiement suspect n’apparaît, il s’agit plus que probablement d’une arnaque. Surtout, ne cédez jamais aux coups de pression et prenez toujours le temps d’analyser une situation.
Autre point particulièrement important : certains arnaqueurs parviennent aujourd’hui à faire apparaître le véritable numéro d’une banque sur le téléphone de leur victime. Pour être plus précis, il est ici question de spoofing, soit une usurpation de numéro de téléphone. Par conséquent, voir le numéro officiel de votre banque s’afficher sur votre smartphone ne signifie en aucun cas que l’appel provient réellement de celle-ci. En fin de compte, le meilleur moyen d’éviter ce type d’arnaque reste tout simplement de couper court à l’appel.

articles.title: JanAI Technology launches with a plan to take AI to 100 million Bharat households
articles.text:
JanAI Technology launches with a plan to take AI to 100 million Bharat households
JanAI Technology plans to bring AI-powered services to 100 million Bharat households through 10,000 local JanAI Cafes in three years.
AI wants to reach the front door of Bharat.
JanAI Technology Private Limited, an impact enterprise under the JanAI movement, has launched with a goal of bringing artificial intelligence-powered services to 100 million households across Bharat over the next three years.
The company will deliver these services through a network of 10,000 JanAI Cafes, which will be run by trained local entrepreneurs. The first version of the platform has gone live across nine JanAI Cafes, including seven launched in Mysuru and Prayagraj districts.
Vishwesh Pai, a product leader and investor with more than two decades of experience across companies including Atlassian, ServiceNow, Amazon and Samsung, has joined JanAI Technology as Co-Founder and CEO. JanAI founder Madan Padaki will serve as Co-Founder and Chief Evangelist, while Head Held High Foundation will be the Community Capability and Resilience Partner.
Taking AI beyond the smartphone
JanAI Technology is not building its own foundation models. Instead, it plans to use open-source and Indic speech models and build technology around the specific needs of communities.
Its platform includes a voice pipeline designed for Indian dialects and noisy rural environments, AI agent orchestration and a consent architecture designed around India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act.
The company is also building services around public digital infrastructure and aims to make government schemes, jobs, finance and other services easier to access through voice.
One of its products, JanAI Asha, is a voice-first assistant that can be accessed through a phone call or two-way app communication in Indian languages. It is designed to work without typing or requiring English.
JanAI Adopt will provide the platform layer for AI agents, knowledge, scheme eligibility and data privacy, while JanAI Bazaar will bring services across finance, health, agriculture, education, jobs, MSMEs and government schemes into one marketplace.
JanAI Cafes bring AI to the last mile
The physical part of the model is the JanAI Cafe.
These cafes will be staffed by trained entrepreneurs from local communities, who will help residents access AI-enabled services and earn a share from the outcomes they facilitate.
The company aims to onboard 100,000 citizens by March 2027. Over three years, it plans to establish cafes across every taluk and build a network of 10,000 cafes.
Madan Padaki said the aim is for each cafe to become an enterprise owned by the community it serves.
“I visualise a JanAI Cafe as an enterprise owned by the village it stands in,” Padaki said. “When a tangible outcome is delivered, the entrepreneur who facilitates it also earns the income.”
The initial services include access to social security benefits, job discovery through the Bluedots model in partnership with EkStep Foundation, and finance through integrations with solutions such as Whatsloan.
Building AI around local needs
Pai said his previous work involved building products for people who already had internet access. JanAI, he said, presents a different challenge.
“I have spent twenty years building products for people who already had the internet,” Pai said. “The harder and more consequential problem will be the next billion who have the connection and still do not have the answer.”
Head Held High Foundation will support the initiative by training local youth as solution creators and helping local entrepreneurs establish and operate JanAI Cafes.
The foundation says it has worked across more than 150 districts over the past 15 years, impacting more than 500,000 households, transforming over 50,000 rural youth and supporting 3,000+ women entrepreneurs.
JanAI Technology’s challenge now is to turn its ambitious target into a sustainable last-mile model. Its approach puts local entrepreneurs between AI and the people it wants to serve, with the company betting that access, language and trust will be as important as the technology itself.

articles.title: Hackers target WordPress sites via third-party WooCommerce plugin
articles.text:
Hackers are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in the WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture premium plugin for WordPress to upload a PHP backdoor.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-27540 and impacts plugin versions 2.0.3.1 and older. It is an unauthenticated arbitrary file-upload vulnerability discovered by security researcher Teemu Saarentaus.
An attacker can exploit it to upload PHP webshells and execute code, potentially leading to a complete site compromise.
From a technical standpoint, the flaw is caused by exposing an unauthenticated AJAX action named wwlc_file_upload_handler, which checks file extensions against an allowlist supplied through the user-controlled file_settings request parameter.
This allows adding ‘php’ to the permitted file types, making the plugin accept PHP executable file uploads.
The vulnerability was addressed in version 2.0.3.2 of the WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture plugin, released on February 20.
However, WordPress security company Defiant is warning that its Wordfence web application firewall blocked over 100,000 attacks linked to CVE-2026-27540.
Wordfence reports that exploitation activity spiked between June 4 and June 17, and on July 1 and August 30.
During the attacks, the hackers upload a webshell that conducts reconnaissance but can also introduce additional payloads.
“The attacker submits a request to the wwlc_file_upload_handler AJAX action containing a forged file_settings parameter and a malicious file with a .php extension,” Wordfence explains.
“The uploaded shell.php is a PHP webshell that reports host details and provides a browser-based upload form for writing additional malicious files to the site.”
Wordfence provides a set of high-offender IP addresses that deployed tens of thousands of exploitation attempts. Administrators are recommended to add them to a blocklist and upgrade to plugin version 2.0.3.2 or later that addresses the security problem.
The researchers advise checking upload directories for unexpected or recently created PHP files, examining logs for requests to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php invoking wwlc_file_upload_handler, and removing unknown administrator accounts.
If compromise is confirmed, the recommended action is to restore the website from a safe backup, as removing all persistence mechanisms, users, and backdoors may be complicated.

articles.title: Renault et Geely accélèrent sur les véhicules électriques au Brésil en renforçant leur alliance - Numerama
articles.text:
C’était la fête à l’usine de Curitiba au Brésil. Le nouvel accord officialisé ce 15 septembre 2026 renforce le partenariat entre Renault et Geely en Amérique latine. Il s’accompagne d’un investissement supplémentaire de 319 millions d’euros.
Pendant longtemps, l’électrification hors des frontières européennes semblait tourner au ralenti. C’est en train de changer. Le Brésil s’électrifie rapidement depuis le début de l’année, avec désormais 7,6 % de part de marché pour les 100 % électriques. L’usine brésilienne de Renault répond à ce nouvel enjeu avec de nouveaux modèles.
Du 100 % électrique Geely dès décembre et un modèle Renault pour 2027
À peine dix mois après une première vague d’annonces, la coentreprise Renault Geely do Brasil (RGdB) franchit un nouveau cap stratégique. L’enveloppe totale d’investissement grimpe désormais à 899 millions d’euros sur la période 2025-2027 (soit 319 millions de plus qu’initialement prévu). Une somme qui permet notamment d’adapter l’outil industriel pour intégrer un futur véhicule électrique signé Renault.
C’est un signal fort qui transforme le site de Curitiba en un véritable hub multi-énergies, capable d’assembler du thermique flex-fuel, de l’hybride et désormais du 100 % électrique de dernière génération.
Concrètement, l’usine brésilienne a modernisé ses chaînes pour intégrer la plateforme moderne GEA (Global Intelligent Electric Architecture) développée par Geely :
- Décembre 2026 : Début de la production du Geely EX2 (Geely E2 en France), une citadine hatchback 100 % électrique qui entend démocratiser l’électrique au Brésil. Elle emboîte le pas au SUV hybride Geely EX5 EM-i, dont la fabrication locale vient d’être lancée.
- Courant 2027 : Arrivée d’un tout nouveau véhicule Renault lui aussi conçu sur la plateforme électrique GEA. Ce modèle inédit sera le premier jalon du plan stratégique FutuREady dans la région, mais il faudra attendre 2027 pour en savoir plus sur ce modèle.
Une réponse pragmatique de Renault pour aller vite
Le choix de la plateforme GEA permet surtout à Renault d’accélérer son offensive électrique au Brésil sans repartir d’une feuille blanche. Le constructeur peut ainsi adapter une architecture existante aux spécificités du marché local et limiter les coûts et la durée de développement. Cela doit aussi permettre à Renault de renforcer son offre face à la progression rapide des constructeurs chinois dans le pays.
Si Renault souhaite encore conserver le secret sur la silhouette et les caractéristiques de son futur modèle de 2027, le partenariat apporte bien plus qu’un simple partage de composants.
Cette annonce montre surtout que l’électrification des marchés émergents n’est plus un sujet secondaire pour les constructeurs, mais une véritable priorité. Si, en Europe, la stratégie du groupe repose sur deux jambes : l’électrique d’un côté, l’hybride de l’autre, au Brésil, les deux jambes s’appellent Renault et Geely. Une formule « gagnant-gagnant », comme l’ont souligné sur place François Provost et Fabrice Cambolive, respectivement directeur général de Renault Group et directeur général de la marque Renault. Et ce n’est que le début.

articles.title: Apple TV et Apple Arcade s'invitent en bonus dans iCloud+ pour ces 20 pays francophones
articles.text:
Apple intègre Apple TV et Apple Arcade à l'abonnement iCloud+ de base, sans supplément de prix, dans plus de 100 pays. Environ une vingtaine de territoires francophones font partie de ce déploiement, lancé ce mois-ci.
Apple ajoute Apple TV et Apple Arcade à l'offre iCloud+ standard, sans coût supplémentaire, dans plus de 100 pays. Le déploiement débute ce mois-ci et touche plusieurs pays francophones, du Maghreb à l'océan Indien.
Du Maroc au Vanuatu, une vingtaine de territoires francophones concernés
L'abonnement iCloud+ combine habituellement stockage en ligne et outils de confidentialité, comme le masquage d'adresse e-mail ou le relais privé. Dans les pays concernés, son palier d'entrée de 50 Go donne désormais accès sans frais supplémentaires au catalogue Apple TV et à plus de 200 jeux Apple Arcade. Le Partage familial permet d'étendre cet accès à cinq autres membres du foyer.
Parmi la liste de plus de 100 pays communiqués par Apple, une vingtaine appartiennent à l'espace francophone. Cela concerne les utilisateurs au Bénin, au Burkina Faso, au Cameroun, au Tchad, en Côte d'Ivoire, en République démocratique du Congo, au Gabon, au Liban, à Madagascar, au Mali, en Mauritanie, à Maurice, au Maroc, au Niger, en République du Congo, au Rwanda, au Sénégal, aux Seychelles, en Tunisie et au Vanuatu.
Pour les utilisateurs déjà abonnés séparément à Apple TV ou à Apple Arcade, la transition est automatique. Leur abonnement individuel est résilié et remplacé par l'accès inclus dans iCloud+, sans perte de progression dans les jeux. Ces deux services ne sont plus vendus à l'unité aux nouveaux clients. Apple One, qui regroupait plusieurs services dans un forfait plus cher, n'est plus proposé aux nouveaux abonnés de ces marchés, même si les abonnements existants restent valables. Certains pays reçoivent en plus un accès à des stations Apple Music Select, une sélection musicale sans publicité.
Ce déploiement s'accompagne d'une extension d'Apple TV, désormais disponible dans 59 pays de plus, pour un total de 170 pays. Le catalogue reste cependant majoritairement anglophone, avec peu de productions locales pour les marchés nouvellement couverts.
- moodRemboursement sous 30 jours
- devices6 connexions simultanées
- live_tvQualité vidéo : Ultra HD (4K)
- downloadLecture hors ligne disponible
- escalator_warningEspace enfant disponible
Apple TV a fait bien du chemin depuis son lancement. Plus ouverte (ne manque plus qu'Android !), mais également plus onéreuse, la plateforme peine encore à justifier un abonnement mensuel fixe tant les ajouts au catalogue sont légers par rapport à la concurrence. Mais, pour une utilisation ponctuelle (ou via Canal+), la solution d'Apple recèle de très (très) bonnes séries qu'il serait dommage de manquer, d'autant que la qualité visuelle proposée est la meilleure de l'industrie.

articles.title: iOS 27 und macOS 27: Warum du mit der Installation nicht warten solltest
articles.text:
iOS 27 und macOS 27: Warum du mit der Installation nicht warten solltest
Apple hat mit iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27, tvOS 27 und visionOS 27 auch zahlreiche Sicherheitslücken geschlossen. Das geht aus der aktualisierten Security-Website des iPhone-Herstellers hervor. Allein für iOS 27 listet Apple mehr als 100 Fehlerbehebungen auf. Auch ältere Systemversionen und der Browser Safari haben Updates bekommen. Immer mehr der Lücken dürften mithilfe von KI gefunden worden sein: Apple nennt unter anderem Anthropic Claude und OpenAI Codex Security, die von Sicherheitsexperten bei der Suche zum Einsatz kamen. Wichtig zu wissen: Nur die jeweils neuesten Systeme erhalten bei Apple sämtliche sicherheitsrelevanten Korrekturen. Außerdem führt das Unternehmen in seinen Listen nur Lücken auf, die Dritte gemeldet haben. Was der Konzern selbst findet und behebt, bleibt unerwähnt.
Angriff per Bluetooth
Laut Apple steckten in den Vorgängerversionen von iOS und iPadOS mindestens zwei Schwachstellen, die sich aus der Ferne angreifen ließen. Eine betrifft das Mobilfunkmodem – das sogenannte Baseband – ab dem iPhone 11. Angreifer konnten dem Handy damit die Netzverbindung nehmen, ein klassischer Denial-of-Service-Angriff. Schwerer wiegt ein Fehler in Bluetooth. Darüber ließ sich sogar beliebiger Code ausführen, außerdem konnten Apps zum Absturz gebracht werden.
Apple hat ansonsten Lücken in nahezu allen wichtigen Teilen des Systems geschlossen. Betroffen sind etwa die Barrierefreiheit, das Dateisystem – hier war das Schreiben in den Kernel-Speicher möglich, also in den geschützten Kern des Betriebssystems – und der App Store, wo ein dauerhafter Account-Identifier den Datenschutz gefährdete. In CoreMedia konnten präparierte Bilder Schadcode ausführen, über Safari ließ sich etwa die Liste installierter Apps auslesen. Dazu kommen mehrere Lücken in WebKit, der Browser-Engine von Safari. Diese behebt Apple mit Safari 27 auch unter macOS Sequoia (15) und Tahoe (26) in Form eines Einzeldownloads (via Software-Update in den Systemeinstellungen). Bereits bekannte Angriffe auf die iPhone- und iPad-Lücken führt Apple nicht auf.
macOS 27 schließt noch mehr Fernangriffe
In macOS 27 hat Apple ähnlich viele Fehler behoben wie in iOS 27. Aus der Ferne angreifbar waren hier sogar mehr Systembereiche: neben der erwähnten Bluetooth-Lücke auch das Drucksystem CUPS sowie insgesamt drei Schwachstellen im Kernel und in der Netzwerkroutine smbx. Eine der Kernel-Lücken konnte den Kernel-Speicher in Mitleidenschaft ziehen, andere führten zu Abstürzen. Über CUPS ließ sich sogar beliebiger Code ausführen.
Viele der erwähnten Lücken hat Apple auch in watchOS 27, visionOS 27 und tvOS 27 geschlossen – sofern die betroffenen Funktionen dort überhaupt vorhanden sind. Zusätzlich hat Apple iOS 26.7, iPadOS 26.7, macOS 26.7 (Tahoe) und macOS 15.8 (Sequoia) veröffentlicht. Diese Versionen enthalten allerdings nicht alle Korrekturen der großen 27er-Updates. Wer ein Gerät besitzt, das die neuen Versionen unterstützt, sollte deshalb überlegen, gleich komplett umzusteigen. Für Intel-Macs gilt das nicht – sie erhalten macOS 27 erst gar nicht mehr.

articles.title: Bose veut équiper les sportifs avec ses écouteurs qui se clipsent sur les oreilles nouvelle génération — Frandroid
articles.text:
Sur le segment des écouteurs, c’est clairement le format qui a le vent dans le dos. En effet, il n’y a pas une marque, audio ou non, qui ne propose ses écouteurs à clipser sur les oreilles. Avant l’arrivée de Samsung sur ce marché avec ses Galay Buds On, Bose ne faisait pas exception et proposait jusqu’ici une seule déclinaison.
    Pour aller plus loin
            Meilleurs écouteurs ouverts en 2026 : le comparatif des open ear
            
Les écouteurs oreilles libres Sport, d’un côté, veulent aider lors d’activités telles que la course à pied, les entraînements et les sorties en plein air, avec un maintien sûr, une grande légèreté et une conception durable en silicone doux.
De l’autre, les écouteurs oreilles libres Ultra 2e génération se présentent comme l’expérience oreilles libres la plus aboutie du fabricant, pensée pour accompagner une journée complète, des transports jusqu’au bureau en passant par les moments de détente.
    Pour aller plus loin
            Écouteurs à clip d’oreille : quand le confort prend le pas sur le son
            
Un format déjà éprouvé
Les deux modèles reprennent le design en forme de manchette dont Bose a été l’un des pionniers sur ce segment. Selon Bose, ce format permet un maintien stable et sans pression, sans obstruer le conduit auditif ni nécessiter de contact ferme avec la tête, à la différence des dispositifs à conduction osseuse. Le son est diffusé directement dans l’air à proximité de l’oreille, ce qui garantirait, selon le fabricant, un rendu plus riche et plus naturel que la vibration osseuse.
La technologie OpenAudio au cœur des deux modèles
Selon le fabricant, la technologie Bose OpenAudio reste le socle commun aux deux nouveautés. Elle fait entrer en jeu un transducteur doté d’une structure acoustique calibrée, de façon à délivrer un son limpide directement à l’oreille tout en limitant au maximum les fuites sonores vers l’extérieur. Le traitement numérique du signal, baptisé Bose SoundDesign, se charge d’équilibrer la clarté des aigus et la profondeur des basses.
Les deux appareils ne proposent volontairement aucune réduction de bruit active. Bose défend l’idée de permettre à l’utilisateur de rester conscient de la circulation, des annonces sonores ou des conversations environnantes, tout en profitant d’une écoute personnelle. Or ce type de réduction de bruit active reste de toute façon très difficile, voire impossible, à intégrer sur des écouteurs à ce format ouvert.
Bose mise également sur sa technologie SpeechClarity, présentée comme une avancée en matière d’isolation vocale optimisée par intelligence artificielle. Un microphone dédié et une unité de captation vocale travaillent de concert dans chaque écouteur afin d’isoler la voix des bruits de fond, tout en conservant son timbre et sa chaleur naturelle, que ce soit dans une rue animée, une gare bondée ou en plein effort physique.
Les écouteurs sport, taillés pour l’effort physique
Les écouteurs oreilles libres Sport misent sur des haut-parleurs dynamiques conçus sur mesure pour un son ample et équilibré, associés à la fonction Auto Volume qui ajuste automatiquement le niveau sonore selon les variations du bruit ambiant. D’après Bose, cette fonction permet par exemple de maintenir un volume constant lorsqu’un coureur passe d’un tronçon silencieux à une rue très fréquentée pendant un entraînement au marathon.
Le maintien s’appuie sur un arceau en forme de C recouvert d’un revêtement mat en silicone doux, pensé pour rester stable lors de mouvements brusques de la tête ou pendant la pratique du vélo. Des boutons physiques texturés permettent de contrôler la musique, les appels et le volume, même avec les doigts moites en plein effort. Les écouteurs proposent une certification IP54, gage de résistance à la transpiration, aux éclaboussures et à la poussière. L’étui de chargement, suffisamment compact pour tenir dans une poche, prend en charge la recharge sans fil et se distingue par un couvercle translucide et texturé.
Sur le plan de l’autonomie, Bose annonce jusqu’à 7 heures de lecture sur une seule charge, complétées par 22 heures supplémentaires grâce à l’étui de recharge. Chaque écouteur pèse 10 grammes, pour un étui de 50 grammes. Les écouteurs Sport sont proposés en Noir et Blanc nuage, ainsi que dans une édition limitée Vert eucalyptus.
Les Ultra Open 2e génération, pensés pour la journée entière
Les écouteurs Ultra 2e génération conservent la silhouette du modèle original, tout en intégrant un nouveau haut-parleur promettant, selon le fabricant, des basses plus profondes et un volume plus élevé que la première génération. La fonction Auto Volume est également présente, ajustant la lecture par exemple lorsque l’utilisateur quitte un café bruyant pour un espace de travail silencieux.
La principale nouveauté est le mode Cinéma, qui repose sur la technologie TrueSpatial de Bose. C’est la même fonction que l’on trouve déjà sur les casques QuietComfort Ultra Headphones 2e génération et QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds 2e génération. Rappelons qu’il est conçu pour les contenus vidéo et les podcasts. Il permet d’élargir l’espace sonore perçu tout en conservant des dialogues nets et centrés, pour une expérience que le fabricant compare à celle d’une salle de projection.
Le son haute qualité et une meilleure autonomie
En outre, notre que les écouteurs bénéficient aussi d’un capuchon métallique revisité à la finition biseautée, et son étui, repensé pour tenir à la verticale, prend désormais en charge la recharge sans fil. Les écouteurs Ultra 2e génération prennent en charge Snapdragon Sound avec aptX Adaptive, pour une latence réduite et une connectivité plus fiable avec les smartphones Android compatibles.
Côté autonomie, Bose promet jusqu’à 9 heures de lecture par charge, complétées de 19,5 heures supplémentaires via l’étui. Les coloris proposés sont le Noir et le Blanc nuage, complétés par trois éditions limitées : Chocolat cerise, Vert olive et Rose ciel. À titre de comparaison, la première génération des Ultra Open Earbuds se limitait à 7 heures d’autonomie par charge et au Bluetooth 5.3, ce qui illustre la progression annoncée sur ce nouveau modèle.
Connectivité et logiciel communs aux deux modèles
Les deux nouveaux modèles d’écouteurs partagent la même base de connectivité, avec le Bluetooth Core 5.4, la prise en charge multipoint pour deux appareils simultanés, ainsi que les codecs SBC et AAC. Google Fast Pair facilite l’appairage rapide avec les terminaux Android. L’application Bose permet de personnaliser l’expérience d’écoute grâce à un égaliseur réglable à trois bandes, au réglage de la fonction Auto Volume et à la configuration de raccourcis, en plus de gérer les appareils Bluetooth et les mises à jour du micrologiciel.
Bose précise qu’une mise à jour du firmware, prévue après le lancement du 1er octobre, ajoutera plusieurs fonctionnalités aux deux modèles : la localisation via Google Find Hub, l’intégration de l’assistant Alexa+ pour des tâches mains libres comme la réservation d’une table ou une recommandation musicale, ainsi que des raccourcis dédiés à Apple Music.
Disponibilité et prix
Les écouteurs Bose Ultra Open Earbuds 2e génération seront disponibles à partir du 1er octobre 2026 au prix de 299,95 euros. Les écouteurs Bose Sport Open suivront le 15 octobre 2026, au tarif de 199,95 euros.

articles.title: Apple's 2027 roadmap includes iPhone 18, iPhone Air 2, and iPhone 18e, all reportedly using the A20 chip
articles.text:
Looking ahead: It's been less than a week since Apple introduced its first foldable and refreshed Pro-grade iPhones, yet attention is already turning to the next chapter. On deck through the first half of 2027 are more than a dozen new products spanning multiple categories.
According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple will enter 2027 with three new iPhones on deck including the iPhone 18, the iPhone Air 2, and the entry-level iPhone 18e. The standard 18 and the Air 2 will be powered by Apple's A20 chip, and the latter will receive a second camera for ultra-wide photography.
Apple also has refreshed iPads ready to go for early next year. A new budget-friendly model will target kids and students, we're told, while updated iPad Pro models will get a chip upgrade and perhaps a vapor chamber cooler for improved thermals. The iPad Air line, meanwhile, will reportedly receive an OLED screen for the first time, plus the usual chip bump.
A pair of new Apple Pencil styluses are also expected to debut around the same time as the updated iPads. These will also be compatible with the new iPhone Duo. On the Mac front, Apple is said to be working on new 13- and 15-inch MacBook Air models as well as a follow-up to the popular MacBook Neo.
It's worth noting that consumers won't have to wait until the calendar rolls over to get new Apple hardware as several additional products are also due out by the end of 2026.
Highlights include a new HomePod mini smart speaker with Siri AI, a long overdue Apple TV refresh with Siri AI, a pair of new high-end touchscreen MacBooks, and a smart-home hub meant to "bring Siri AI to life." There's also a new version of the iPad mini on deck, plus a new iMac, and an updated entry-level MacBook Pro.
It's too early to know how newly minted CEO John Ternus will do at Apple, but he's certainly coming out of the gate with a slew of new products for the masses.

articles.title: Steam Deck 2 Plans Haven't Changed Despite RAM Crisis, Claims Valve
articles.text:
Tuesday, September 15th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Steam Deck 2 Plans Haven't Changed Despite RAM Crisis, Claims Valve
Valve has confirmed that the ongoing DRAM shortage hasn't changed anything about its plans for a Steam Deck 2, even though the crisis has driven up prices on the company's other hardware. Speaking with IGN's Jacqueline Thomas, Valve developer Pierre-Loup Griffais was asked directly whether the memory shortage had affected the next handheld's development. Here's what he told IGN:
"We've talked before about how we want to make sure there's a very delineated performance improvement for something like a future Steam Deck, and I think we're still looking at it in the same way. It's just a matter of looking at the current conditions and seeing how and when we can deliver something like that. But from what we're working on, as far as the user experience goes and what the product that we're trying to build goes, it's very similar goals."
It is important to remember the context behind Valve's recent hardware launches. The Steam Machine ended up at $1,049 for its base model, and the Steam Frame launched at $1,059, both well above what Valve had reportedly hoped to charge before memory prices spiked. Griffais admitted pricing has likely dented demand for those two products, though he said it's hard to quantify how much. For the Steam Deck 2, Valve says the crisis hasn't had a significant impact on development plans, at least for now. That pressure might eventually reach the Steam Deck 2, since its release is still some ways away and Valve still hasn't given any indication of a launch window yet.
		
		Source:
				Valve via IGN			
	
	
	
		
	
		
"We've talked before about how we want to make sure there's a very delineated performance improvement for something like a future Steam Deck, and I think we're still looking at it in the same way. It's just a matter of looking at the current conditions and seeing how and when we can deliver something like that. But from what we're working on, as far as the user experience goes and what the product that we're trying to build goes, it's very similar goals."
8 Comments on Steam Deck 2 Plans Haven't Changed Despite RAM Crisis, Claims Valve
Of course the current ram crisis doesn’t affect it.
In this thread:
“BREAKING: Fresh water fisherman confirms rising salt water tides not affecting his trip plans.”
Valve's hardware plans for the (delayed) Steam Machine and the Frame were probably too far advanced to put a stop to it when the memory crisis hit but they certainly won't even consider a Deck 2 in this market for a long time to come.
Valve were not developing a new Steam deck currently, and now they are not developing it even harder? :rolleyes:
There are cycles in gaming hardwares, some are incremental (ada lovelace to blackwell), others are far more ambitious. Whilst there are tremendous delays and challenges because of AI shortages and inflation, I believe we are near a big jump for handheld with the PS6 era coming soon (ML upscaling, Zen 6, efficiency improvement etc.)
Going Intel will be a bit limiting, even with XeSS. Going Intel or AMD will have to contend with x86 performance/watt. They could go Nvidia but outside Nintendo that seems kinda... yeah. If they went with another ARM based CPU chip, they will miss out on things like upscaling and FG due to lack of software support from these other manufactures.
I imagine that they would stick with AMD, but their SKUs are really restrictive compared to the catalog book that Intel offers. But Exynos might give them a solid performance/watt over x86. And whatever RDNA mods Samsung has done to make it more mobile chip friendly on the power side, if any.

articles.title: GM gives its most important trucks a new UI—and includes CarPlay
articles.text:
General Motors is about to launch new versions of its bestselling Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra pickup trucks for model year 2027, and among the changes are new user interfaces for the trucks’ digital displays. The automaker has gone for a more minimalist approach than we’ve seen from it in the past, and after a demo yesterday, it seems like it has been listening to constructive feedback to improve the products. And yes, unlike GM’s electric vehicles, these trucks still let you cast your Apple or Android phone to the infotainment system.
Although GM showed us video of the main instrument cluster—the gauges and info that’s presented to the driver—we don’t have any screenshots we can show you. But I was impressed with the restraint and lack of visual noise; instead, the background is always black, which should be dark even at night thanks to local dimming technology.
There are a number of different views. One with simple half-moon dials for speed and engine rpm; on the right side of the display is a user-configurable zone, where you can browse your music or audio feeds, display trip info, or turn-by-turn directions. Another is a driver assist display, with green as the highlight color to show when Super Cruise is active; this shows you a representation of what the car’s fused sensors are seeing around it. A third is for off-road driving, with your various angles and diff settings, and a fourth is for towing.
Note the real controls for the HVAC.
Credit:
GM
Note the real controls for the HVAC.
Credit:
GM
But there’s also an even more minimalist version that simply shows the speed as big white digits and nothing else. This is similar to the night mode you’d find in Saabs, and it’s very useful for night driving.
At the base of the main instrument display is a strip of information that’s permanently displayed regardless of the view mode you choose—this includes things like your fuel level, the drive mode, and any warning lights that may appear.
Yes, it has CarPlay
The central infotainment screen still runs on Android Automotive OS, but now the home screen is a more useful split view showing the music and navigation apps, with a full map view rather than the limited map that GM previously showed in its split-screen view. “If you wanted to search something or provide feedback on road conditions or something like that, when you tapped on the screen, it took you out of the home screen and took you to the full-screen maps. Here, you can do everything that full-screen maps can do right inside this window,” said Colin McCormick, group product manager at GM.
A dedicated row at the bottom of the screen is for the climate controls, although, as you’ll note from the photos, there are physical dials to change the temperature, as well as physical buttons for fan speed and demisting.
GM has also integrated more Android-like notifications into the infotainment system and included the ability to create quick actions. It has also changed the behavior of some of its apps—now, if you accept a phone call, it won’t switch you out of whatever app was active to dump you into the dialer app anymore.
Here’s what Apple CarPlay looks like. The card on the left shows towing information.
GM
Here’s what Apple CarPlay looks like. The card on the left shows towing information.
GM
Here’s what Android Auto looks like. Here, the card shows trip info.
GM
Here’s what Android Auto looks like. Here, the card shows trip info.
GM
Here’s what Apple CarPlay looks like. The card on the left shows towing information.
GM
Here’s what Android Auto looks like. Here, the card shows trip info.
GM
GM made the decision to drop Apple CarPlay and Android Auto phone casting from its newer EVs, and it’s one we’ve been pretty critical of. Although the automaker told us it made that decision in order to offer a better, more unified experience to its customers, that may well have changed: here, customers still have the choice to just cast their phone to the center screen.
And it has done a better job of integrating CarPlay and Android Auto into the experience, putting the casting apps in a large window or tile that takes up most but not all of the infotainment screen. To the left is another card that allows you to access other native apps, like towing or music (although you can still have CarPlay as the source for that native music app, should you start feeling a little Inceptionish). Porsche took a similar approach to working with, rather than against, users who enjoy CarPlay, and this looks like a welcome step from GM.
GM’s spokesperson wouldn’t be drawn on whether this means we’re going to see a corporate retreat from the previous stance on EVs, but I will note that the press release it sent Ars does say that the system was built “as a single scalable foundation across electric, gas and diesel-powered vehicles, it transforms time spent behind the wheel into an effortless, personalized journey,”—emphasis mine.
Passenger screens are here to stay
Complaining about the trend of OEMs putting an extra infotainment screen in the dash for the front passenger is evidently a losing battle now, because such a feature will be available on the Sierra and Silverado. The screen is coated in a polarized filter, so the driver can’t see what they’re doing or watch what they’re watching.
There are lots of native streaming apps now. The lower trim piece folds down to show more of the screen.
Credit:
GM
There are lots of native streaming apps now. The lower trim piece folds down to show more of the screen.
Credit:
GM
This can be streaming content or video piped in via HDMI from a port down by the passenger’s knee. And the passenger infotainment screen will pair with Bluetooth headphones so the driver doesn’t necessarily have to listen to whatever it is, either. (Some information will show up on the main infotainment screen, so the driver will have an idea of what content is playing on the screen and decide whether to pass through audio to the truck’s speakers, GM told us.) It’s not just for watching video, though—there’s even a full web browser, and you can use your smartphone as a keyboard or input device.
Jonathan is the Automotive Editor at Ars Technica. He has a BSc and PhD in Pharmacology. In 2014 he decided to indulge his lifelong passion for the car by leaving the National Human Genome Research Institute and launching Ars Technica's automotive coverage. He lives in Washington, DC.

articles.title: iPhone 17 Pro entra em oferta após iPhone 18 Pro ser homologado • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
iPhone 17 Pro entra em oferta após iPhone 18 Pro ser homologado
Durante a pré-venda do iPhone 18 Pro, o iPhone 17 Pro (256 GB) com tela OLED de 120 Hz e câmeras de 48 MP sai 30% mais barato no Pix no Magazine Luiza
O iPhone 17 Pro de 256 GB está saindo por R$ 8.048 no Pix no Magazine Luiza. O smartphone da Apple com tela OLED de 120 Hz e câmeras de 48 MP recebe desconto de 30% sobre o preço original de R$ 11.499, às vésperas da chegada do novo iPhone 18 Pro às lojas.
O iPhone 17 Pro possui elementos em comum com o novo iPhone 18 Pro, sendo a grande diferença as câmeras: embora o kit principal dos dois celulares tenha sensores de 48 MP, o modelo mais recente ostenta aberturas de lente variáveis na wide com OIS, ultrawide e telefoto com zoom óptico de 4x. A frontal Center Stage de 18 MP é a mesma em ambos.
Outra diferença é o chip interno, sendo o A19 Pro no iPhone 17 Pro e o A20 Pro de 2 nm no 18 Pro, que promete 20% mais desempenho em CPU e 40% mais na GPU que a geração anterior. Ambos contam com 12 GB de RAM e 256 GB de armazenamento.
A tela Super Retina XDR OLED de 6,3″ é a mesma em ambos, com ProMotion de 120 Hz e brilho de até 3.000 nits, que reproduz imagens com cores vibrantes e alta fluidez nas transições, além de ter visibilidade garantida em qualquer ambiente.
O corpo de alumínio do iPhone 17 Pro e do iPhone 18 Pro, este recentemente homologado para venda no Brasil, conta com o vidro Ceramic Shield 2 de ambos os lados, resistente a pancadas e quedas. A certificação IP68 adiciona proteção em cenários como poeira intensa e mergulhos acidentais.
A bateria do iPhone 18 Pro possui 4.056 mAh contra 3.998 mAh de seu antecessor, que oferecem 36 horas e 31 horas de reprodução de vídeo respectivamente, segundo a fabricante. O modelo mais recente recebe uma carga de 50% em 15 minutos via USB-C, contra 20 minutos do 17 Pro.
O iPhone 17 Pro de 256 GB (R$ 8.048 no Pix) roda iOS 26, enquanto o novo iPhone 18 Pro sai rodando o iOS 27 da caixa. Ambos possuem conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0 e NFC.

articles.title: Developer builds viral 3D source code visualizer that consumes 21GB of RAM — flies around 2.5 million lines of code at over 120 frames per second
articles.text:
Developer builds viral 3D source code visualizer that consumes 21GB of RAM — flies around 2.5 million lines of code at over 120 frames per second
He was so preoccupied about whether he could, he didn't stop to think about whether he should.
The immortal line "it's a Unix system, I know this" is forever entrenched in many a techie's brain. In the Jurassic Park movie, the visualization software in question was Silicon Graphics' File System Navigator for IRIX, an actual piece of software running on a real SG workstation. The concept of viewing files in 3D space never truly caught on, but the horsepower available in contemporary machines may change that. Makepad creator Rik Arends created his own 3D flyable source code visualizer that he claims handles 2.5 million lines with ease, at 120+ FPS, no less.
Although the published video is only at 60 FPS due to X's limitation, the navigation looks smooth indeed, and it's impressive to see all the actual source code in a reasonably readable manner. Arends says the visualization initially took 21 GB of RAM (in this economy?!), but that after judicious application of indexes and streaming compression, he got memory usage down to a much more palatable 3.5 GB. Although he remarked that he's yet to fully optimize the visualizer, he did try to load Chromium's entire source tree (51 million lines) in only 60 seconds at one point.
While one can argue that the 3D visualization of the code itself is probably really fun to look at, its practical use is also questionable, at least as-is. A commenter remarked that adding a time element would help immensely, by displaying changes to the source files. 3D tracking of dependencies would probably be handy, too. There's already an actual full-fledged commercial tool called CodeCharta that visualizes changes and hotspots in 3D, though the flybys aren't quite as impressive.
Arends says that he intends to turn this visualization tool into a product and charge a small fee for it, though he admits that the usefulness of the visualization may be limited. When asked why he created this, he simply said, "because I could." The jury is still out on whether he should.

articles.title: Fixing banking’s omnichannel blind spot: Why the physical branch needs a digital brain - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Fixing banking’s omnichannel blind spot: Why the physical branch needs a digital brain
For years, retail banking strategy followed a predictable script: Shift routine transactions to digital channels, downsize physical footprints and route customer service inquiries to centralized contact centers. The underlying assumption was that physical branches were dying embers of a bygone era.
Yet industry data tells a radically different story. According to the 2026 Future of Branch Banking Report by the Digital Banking Report, 71% of financial institutions consider branches mission-critical or very important to long-term growth. Only 3% plan to shrink their networks, while 97% are actively investing in, modernizing or expanding their physical footprints. Physical centers haven’t vanished; their core purpose has simply evolved.
Customers no longer visit a branch to deposit a check or check a balance — they handle those tasks on their smartphones. Today, customers walk through a branch door during life’s most complex, sensitive and high-stakes financial moments: applying for a mortgage, opening a commercial business account, navigating estate planning or resolving a critical fraud incident.
Despite millions invested in digital transformation, retail banking still faces a major operational blind spot: the disconnected branch experience. While contact centers and mobile apps have gradually consolidated into unified customer experience platforms, physical financial centers remain digitally isolated. When an information technology strategy leaves the physical branch out of the enterprise telemetry loop, both customer experience and operational efficiency suffer.
The core problem: Frontline blind spots and institutional amnesia
To understand why banking customer experience breaks down, look at the typical customer journey preceding a branch visit:
- A customer browses home loan options on a mobile banking app.
- Unsure about specific rates, they dial the contact center and speak to an agent for 10 minutes before getting disconnected or deciding to visit in person.
- They walk into their local branch 30 minutes later to finish the process.
What happens when they sit down at the banker’s desk? The banker starts from scratch. “How can I help you today?” asks the representative, unaware of the app’s browsing history or the prior call. The customer is forced to repeat their story, restate their information and re-verify their identity. This phenomenon, institutional amnesia, erodes customer trust at the very moment it matters most.
This friction stems from four persistent execution gaps in banking technology architecture:
- The data gap: Customer interaction history is siloed across core engines, digital banking platforms and contact centers. Branch-level workstations rarely receive this context in real time, tracking account balances without capturing real-time intent.
- The workflow gap: Processes do not connect across channels. A mortgage or loan journey started online halts as soon as the customer walks into a physical center.
- The employee enablement gap: Legacy branch systems were designed for tellers processing transactions, not advisers delivering consultation. Frontline staff act as highly paid human ATMs rather than trusted advisors because they lack real-time guidance tools and context overlays.
- The measurement gap: While every click, scroll and call-center drop-off is meticulously analyzed by enterprise data teams, in-person interactions vanish into an analytics black hole, judged by transaction counts that no longer reflect the real value of branches.
According to the Future of Branch Banking Report, 38% of operations leaders cite inconsistent execution across markets as their top operational risk. When service quality varies by branch, the institution bears hidden operational liability.
Bridging the gap: Real-world ROI and connected architecture
Solving this challenge requires expanding the definition of “omnichannel” so that context flows seamlessly across all touchpoints, regardless of medium or physical location. Modern platform launches, such as Talkdesk Inc. for Financial Centers built on the Customer Experience Automation framework, demonstrate how cloud-native software layers can integrate physical bank branches directly into the enterprise contact center ecosystem.
By consolidating fragmented systems and surfacing AI guidance across all touchpoints, financial institutions are achieving dramatic, quantifiable returns:
- Merchants Bank: A 150-year-old community institution replaced static paper reference binders with AI-powered knowledge management and unified phone, chat, SMS, and email. The shift enabled the team to answer 90% of calls within 20 seconds, capture 50% of calls on the unified platform, and extend customer support around the clock.
- TowneBank: As TowneBank scaled across Virginia and the Carolinas, it unified customer relationship management across all departments with real-time AI assistance. By reducing administrative friction for staff, it successfully navigated major system conversions while achieving a 97% satisfaction rate and a 4.8 overall CSAT.
- Arbella Insurance: In property and casualty insurance, Arbella deployed a unified CX platform to 1,000+ employees and agency partners in ten months. They improved service levels by 20% within weeks, raised CSAT by 3%, and reduced average handle times by 15 to 45 seconds — generating an estimated $1.7 million in savings over three years.
These real-world outcomes demonstrate three immediate operational advantages of unifying intelligence across the customer service ecosystem, including physical channels:
- Instant journey continuity: Frontline workers receive a unified workspace that surfaces recent app searches, contact center transcripts, open tickets and intent signals. The banker begins the conversation at step four rather than step one.
- In-flight AI copilot guidance: As bankers transition to universal advisers, AI copilots run in the background, surfacing compliant scripts, next-best-action prompts and automated summary notes, enabling advisers to focus on listening rather than typing.
- Centralized telemetry and the “neighborhood P&L”: Capturing branch visit intent, outcomes and customer feedback builds a complete 360-degree dataset. This enables institutions to move beyond counting teller transactions and adopt a “Neighborhood P&L” — giving branches credit for total ecosystem revenue generated, even when a customer signs the final loan application at home on a tablet.
Recommendations for banking IT leaders
For CIOs, enterprise architects, and technology directors in financial services, modernizing the branch network requires a clear shift in infrastructure strategy.
1. Treat the branch as an active telemetry edge
Stop treating physical branches as isolated IT footprints limited to local networks, security cameras, and core banking terminals. Modernize branch architecture by establishing event-driven application programming interfaces that feed in-person interaction data (visit reasons, appointment notes, outcomes) directly into your centralized data cloud or customer relationship management system alongside digital telemetry.
2. Unify contact center and branch workspaces
Avoid buying point solutions that create new software silos. Look for lightweight cloud layers that allow branch staff and contact center agents to operate within the same unified desktop workspace. Operating on shared context engines and AI copilots lowers training costs, reduces desktop software bloat and eliminates channel data discrepancies.
3. Enforce real-time identity resolution at check-in
Journey continuity relies on immediate identification. Implement branch check-in capabilities — via mobile app geofencing, QR codes or self-service kiosks — that instantly match arriving customers with their digital profiles and trigger real-time context alerts on banker desktops before the customer takes a seat.
4. Deploy AI with financial-grade compliance guardrails
Branch advisers handle sensitive, highly regulated financial discussions. When deploying AI-driven next-best-action engines or real-time assistant tools to frontline staff, ensure the platform includes built-in compliance guardrails that adhere strictly to local banking regulations, fair lending rules and customer privacy preferences.
Final thoughts
The physical branch is far from obsolete, but its role as an isolated, standalone brick-and-mortar building is over. Physical locations represent a structural advantage that digital-native neobanks cannot quickly replicate.
For IT leaders in financial services, the strategic mandate is clear: stop separating digital channels from physical spaces. By linking branch interactions into the broader CX automation strategy, financial institutions remove longstanding customer friction, empower frontline advisers and transform physical footprints into connected relationship hubs.
